app.name: Gusto App Integrations API app (your own OAuth app)

verdict.summary: Creating a sandbox OAuth app is quick, but production access is gated: Gusto's API is restricted to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners, and production keys require an approved Production Pre-Approval, a Security Review, a Partner Checklist and QA. Gusto publishes no review timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for the sandbox setup (estimate); the production path is several days to weeks of applications, security evidence and follow-up (estimate, no timeline published).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 1-2 hours to a sandbox OAuth test with a demo company (estimate), if your business is eligible for the API.
verdict.approval_wait: Not published by Gusto. One third-party connector guide says Gusto typically responds to Pre-Approval within 1-2 weeks (unverified).

gates.name: Developer Portal sandbox (works for you)
gates.unlocks: Create a Developer Portal account and an Application, get sandbox client_id and client_secret, and connect a demo company through your own OAuth flow.
limits: Developer Portal keys are sandbox-only at first (api.gusto-demo.com).
Requires a Developer Portal account before the Pre-Approval application can be completed.
Gusto recommends applying for Pre-Approval before building; building first is at your own risk.

gates.name: Demo environment with test companies (invited/test users)
gates.unlocks: Test OAuth and API calls against demo companies, including scope testing, before any real customer data is involved.
limits: Scopes are not enforced in demo; out-of-scope calls succeed there but return 403 in production.
Only primary or full-access admins at a customer company can authorize a new app.
Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes; access tokens expire after 2 hours.
Rate limit is 200 requests per minute per OAuth grant.
No install cap or user-count limit for unreviewed apps was found in the docs (not confirmed).
Without an approved Pre-Approval, Gusto gives no implementation support, debugging help or design guidance.
The API is currently restricted to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners; non-partners should use the Gusto CLI or MCP server for their own company.
gates.time_to_reach: Same session as Gate 1 once the app exists

gates.name: Production (works for anyone, after Gusto approval)
gates.unlocks: Production API keys and real customer companies once Pre-Approval, Security Review, Partner Checklist and QA are passed and Gusto configures your scopes.
limits: Production keys are issued only after QA, through the Developer Portal.
Production redirect URI changes go through Gusto support email.
Scope changes after production are requested by email to Gusto support.
Some scopes (e.g. payroll_digests) must be enabled by a Gusto representative.
No separate marketplace or listing review is documented; Gusto features integrated partners in its directory as a visibility benefit.
gates.time_to_reach: Not published by Gusto. Third-party source: Pre-Approval response in 1-2 weeks (unverified). Security Review and QA timing unknown.

steps.title: Check that the Gusto App Integrations API fits your business
steps.detail: Confirm you build a software product for businesses with an integration for shared customers, and that your product has a track record with small businesses. Gusto restricts the API to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners. If you only need to connect your own Gusto company, use the Gusto CLI or MCP server instead of an OAuth app.
gotchas: Gusto's consumer payroll UI is not the target of this guide.
Embedded Payroll has its own docs and partner path; this guide assumes App Integrations. Confirm which product you are building for.

steps.title: Create a Developer Portal account
steps.detail: Sign up at dev.gusto.com. You need this account before you can complete the Production Pre-Approval application. The docs do not mention a paid plan, partner fee or business verification at this step.
gotchas: The developer portal sits behind a bot check for automated access; complete it in a normal browser.

steps.title: Complete Organization setup and create an Application
steps.detail: In the Developer Portal, complete your Organization setup, then create an Application. The Application generates a client_id and client_secret for the sandbox. Store the client_secret securely; it is needed for the Composio connection.
gotchas: Developer Portal keys are sandbox-only at first (api.gusto-demo.com).
Exact form field labels were not captured in research; check the screen when you create the app.

steps.title: Register the redirect URI on the Application
steps.detail: Add the Composio callback URL as a redirect URI on your Application. Gusto requires at least one redirect URI and allows several on one app. Wildcards and URIs with fragments (#) are rejected. Demo redirects can be edited in the Applications tab.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Production redirect changes go through Gusto support email, so get this right in the sandbox.
Paste the exact URL from your Composio auth config; do not retype it.

steps.title: Create the Gusto auth config in Composio with your own credentials
steps.detail: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Gusto, so you must supply your own client_id and client_secret. Enter them in the Gusto auth config in Composio. Gusto's authorize and token endpoints are used by the flow.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Test the OAuth flow with a demo company
steps.detail: Create a demo company in the Gusto sandbox. Connect it through your Composio auth config, signing in as a primary or full-access admin. Choose the company during authorization if your user manages several. Exchange the code within 10 minutes; the flow fails if it expires.
gotchas: Only primary or full-access admins can authorize a new app.
Authorization codes are valid for 10 minutes.
Access tokens expire after 2 hours; test refresh behavior, since refresh token lifetime is not documented.

steps.title: Decide the scope list and test each scope in demo
steps.detail: Draft the minimum set of scopes your integration needs, named as resource:action (for example employees:read). Gusto assigns scopes per app during review, so this list is a request, not a guarantee. Make a call for each scope in the demo environment, because demo does not enforce scopes and will not reveal missing ones.
gotchas: Scopes Gusto assigns must be tested in demo and are enforced in production; out-of-scope calls return 403.
Composio's default scopes (companies:read, employees:read, payrolls:read) may not match what Gusto assigns; confirm the names against the Gusto API reference.

steps.title: Set the API version header and verify token scopes
steps.detail: Send the X-Gusto-API-Version: 2026-06-15 header on API calls. Call GET /v1/token_info with a demo token to confirm which scopes it holds. The v2025-06-15 version is retired after November 15, 2026, so do not build against it.
gotchas: Today is 2026-10-28; v2025-06-15 stops working after November 15, 2026.

steps.title: Submit the Production Pre-Approval application
steps.detail: Apply for Production Pre-Approval through the Developer Portal. Gusto recommends applying before you invest in a build, and says approval is not guaranteed. Information you submit is handled under Gusto's Developer Terms. The application is a Qualtrics form whose full contents were not captured in research.
gotchas: Gusto says building before approval is at your own risk.
Gusto's docs do not list common rejection reasons.

steps.title: Draft Security Review materials
steps.detail: Draft answers for the Security Review: security and privacy audits (such as SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS), any penetration test report, security and incident-response contacts, and policies. If you have no formal audit, prepare answers on MFA, encryption, vulnerability scanning and any bug bounty program. A person must supply the real audit documents and contacts.
gotchas: The Pre-Approval application may already contain enough for this review, but Gusto may ask for more.
The penetration test report is a named input Gusto asks for.

steps.title: Respond to Gusto follow-up questions
steps.detail: Gusto's GRC team starts the Security Review after Pre-Approval, and direct integrators are emailed next steps. Answer any follow-up questions promptly. The Security Review is on hold until Gusto gets your response.
gotchas: A third-party source says Gusto may ask follow-up questions during its security review.

steps.title: Complete the Partner Checklist and pass QA
steps.detail: After Pre-Approval is approved, Gusto grants access to the Partner Checklist. Complete it and share it with Gusto. Gusto requires a quality review (QA) and an approved Pre-Approval for all builds using its API.
gotchas: The Partner Checklist is available only after Pre-Approval is approved.
No QA timeline is published.

steps.title: Wait for Gusto to issue production credentials and scopes
steps.detail: After QA, Gusto issues production credentials through the Developer Portal and configures your scopes. Merge's guide says Gusto provisions production credentials and sets scopes for approved partners. Once you receive them, replace the sandbox client_id and client_secret in your Composio auth config.
gotchas: Production keys are not issued before approval; there is no self-serve path.

steps.title: Confirm production scopes and update the public listing
steps.detail: Check your granted scopes in the Developer Portal and retest one call per scope in production. Request scope changes by email to Gusto support. Update your website or marketplace and publish support content; Gusto will feature integrated partners in its directory.
gotchas: Out-of-scope calls return 403 Forbidden in production.
Gusto's directory feature is a visibility benefit, not a review requirement.

requirements.detail: Required before the Production Pre-Approval application can be completed. No paid plan or business verification is mentioned in the docs.

requirements.item: Redirect URI registered on the Application
requirements.detail: At least one per app; several allowed. Wildcards and fragments are not supported. Production changes go through Gusto support email.
Information submitted in Pre-Approval is handled under Gusto's Developer Terms.

requirements.item: Only primary or full-access admins can authorize
requirements.detail: End users must be primary or full-access admins at their company to authorize your app. Users with several companies must pick one during authorization.
Authorization code valid 10 minutes. Access token expires after 2 hours. Refresh token lifetime and rotation are not documented.
200 requests per minute on a rolling 60-second window per OAuth grant. No lower limit for unreviewed apps is documented.
Required before production keys are issued or Gusto provides implementation support, QA review or production keys. Approval is not guaranteed.

Run by Gusto's GRC team after Pre-Approval. Inputs include security and privacy audits (e.g. SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS), a penetration test report, security and incident-response contacts, and policies. Without a formal audit, Gusto asks about MFA, encryption, vulnerability scanning and a bug bounty program.
Partner Checklist is granted after Pre-Approval approval and must be completed and shared with Gusto. QA is required for all API builds.
Software product serving businesses, with an integration for shared customers, in a supported category. Early-stage products without a small-business track record are not currently supported.

scopes.effect: Gusto assigns scopes per app during review. Test each one in demo; the granted set may differ from these defaults. Exact names not yet checked against the Gusto API reference.
Gusto recommends requesting only the minimum needed. Scopes not in your granted set return 403 in production. No sensitive or restricted tier is documented.
Gated: a Gusto representative must enable them before use. Plan for a support request if you need them.
Requested by email to Gusto support. Current granted scopes are visible in the Developer Portal.

blockers.symptom: Gusto gives no production keys and no implementation or QA support.
blockers.cause: Production Pre-Approval has not been approved. Gusto issues production keys only after Pre-Approval, Security Review and QA.
blockers.fix: Submit the Production Pre-Approval application early, before heavy build work. Do not plan launch dates until Pre-Approval is approved.
blockers.contact: Gusto App Integrations team via the Developer Portal (email address not captured in research)

blockers.symptom: Your business cannot get API access at all.
blockers.cause: The App Integrations API is restricted to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners, and Gusto's fit criteria exclude early-stage products.
blockers.fix: Confirm eligibility before building. If you only need your own Gusto company, use the Gusto CLI or MCP server instead.
blockers.contact: Gusto support via the Developer Portal

blockers.cause: Gusto's Security Review is on hold until you answer its follow-up questions.
blockers.fix: Monitor the email from Gusto's GRC team and answer follow-up questions quickly. Have audit reports, a penetration test and incident contacts ready.

blockers.symptom: API calls return 403 Forbidden in production but succeed in demo.
blockers.cause: Scopes are not enforced in demo, but production enforces the scopes Gusto assigned. The call used a scope you were not granted.
blockers.fix: Check granted scopes in the Developer Portal and with GET /v1/token_info. Request the missing scope from Gusto support, and test every scope in demo before approval.

blockers.cause: Gusto's rate limit is 200 requests per minute per OAuth grant (rolling 60-second window).
blockers.fix: Throttle calls per user token and back off on errors. No lower limit for unreviewed apps is documented.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Gusto, so you must register your own Gusto Application and paste its client_id and client_secret into the Composio auth config. Gusto assigns scopes per app during review, so the scopes you get may differ from Composio's defaults. Use the Composio callback URL shown in your auth config as the Redirect URI in Gusto.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit lookup reports no managed OAuth for Gusto, so the developer must register their own Gusto app and supply its client credentials.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available": false

evidence.claim: Security Review inputs Gusto asks for include security and privacy audits (such as SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, or PCI DSS), a penetration test report, security and incident-response contacts, and policies. Without a formal audit, Gusto asks about controls such as MFA, encryption, vulnerability scanning, and a bug bounty program.
evidence.quote: Penetration test report(s)

evidence.claim: Gusto says the Pre-Approval application usually contains enough information for the Security Review, but it may ask for more. Until it responds, the Security Review is on hold.
evidence.quote: Your Security Review will be put on hold until we receive a response.

evidence.claim: After Pre-Approval, Gusto's GRC team starts the Security Review. Direct integrators are emailed the next steps; Unified API partners are notified by the partner platform.
evidence.quote: our GRC team will then kick off your Security Review.

evidence.claim: For Integrated Apps, the review requires the Partner Checklist. Access to that checklist is granted only after Pre-Approval is approved, and the completed checklist is shared with Gusto.
evidence.quote: If your Production Pre-Approval is approved, you'll be granted access to our Partner Checklist.

evidence.claim: Gusto's listed fit criteria: a software product serving businesses with an integration for shared customers, in a supported category. Early-stage products that have not yet built a track record with small businesses are not currently supported.
evidence.quote: Early-stage products still establishing a track record of serving small businesses.

evidence.claim: The App Integrations API is currently restricted to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners. A Gusto customer who wants to connect their own company should use the Gusto CLI or MCP server instead of an OAuth app.
evidence.quote: The Gusto API is currently restricted to Gusto App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners.

evidence.claim: The documented review for App Integrations is a QA plus Pre-Approval process, not a public app-directory listing review. No review timeline is published.
evidence.quote: Gusto requires a quality review ("QA") and an approved Production Pre-Approval application for all builds using our API

evidence.claim: Gusto assigns API scopes to each app during review based on its integration use case. The assigned scopes must be tested in demo and are enforced in production, and any call outside them is rejected.
evidence.quote: These scopes must be tested in our demo environment and will be enforced in our production environment upon approval.

evidence.claim: Scope changes after production are requested by emailing Gusto's support address. Assigned scopes can be viewed in the Developer Portal.
evidence.quote: You can check your app’s granted API scopes via your Developer Portal account.

evidence.claim: Scopes are not enforced in the demo environment, so out-of-scope calls succeed there but return 403 Forbidden in production. GET /v1/token_info shows which scopes a token holds.
evidence.quote: Requests outside assigned scopes succeed in demo but return 403 Forbidden in production.

evidence.claim: Gusto's own docs state production access is gated: an approved Production Pre-Approval and a Security Review are required before production keys are issued.
evidence.quote: Production access is gated, and not all applications are approved.

evidence.claim: Some scopes are gated. Gusto's payroll digests changelog says the new payroll_digests scopes must be enabled by a Gusto representative before use.
evidence.quote: These scopes are gated.

evidence.claim: Gusto names scopes by resource and action (e.g. employees:read, employees:write) and recommends requesting only the minimum needed. No sensitive or restricted scope tier and no separate scope review step is documented.
evidence.quote: It’s recommended to limit the scopes you need to the bare minimum

evidence.claim: The authorize step sends the user to https://api.gusto.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, and response_type=code. The code is then exchanged at https://api.gusto.com/oauth/token using client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, and code.
evidence.quote: https://api.gusto.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code

evidence.claim: The authorization code expires 10 minutes after it is issued and must be exchanged for a token before then.
evidence.quote: The authorization code is valid for 10 minutes.

evidence.claim: Access tokens expire after 2 hours, per the Embedded Payroll quickstart. Refresh token lifetime and rotation are not stated in the pages fetched.
evidence.quote: Access tokens expire after 2 hours.

evidence.claim: Only primary or full-access admins at a customer company can authorize a new app. Some users manage several companies and must choose which one to connect during authorization.
evidence.quote: Only primary or full-access admins can authorize new apps.

evidence.claim: The Gusto API rate limit is 200 requests per minute, counted over a rolling 60-second window per OAuth grant (per access token). No lower limit for unreviewed or unlisted apps is documented.
evidence.quote: The Gusto API rate limit is currently 200 requests per minute.

evidence.claim: No install cap or user-count limit for unreviewed or unlisted Gusto apps was found in the docs, changelogs, or search results checked. The docs only describe the gated production approval.
Gusto's API version is selected with the X-Gusto-API-Version header. v2026-06-15 is the current stable release.
evidence.quote: Set the X-Gusto-API-Version: 2026-06-15 header to use it.

evidence.claim: API version v2025-06-15 is retired after November 15, 2026; after that date, requests on that version stop working.
evidence.quote: After November 15, 2026, API version v2025-06-15 will be retired and become unusable

evidence.claim: Without an approved Pre-Approval, Gusto will not provide implementation support, QA review, or production keys.
evidence.quote: Without that approval, we cannot provide implementation support, QA review, or issue production keys.

evidence.claim: Gusto's Developer Portal (dev.gusto.com) returned a bot-check page (HTTP 403) to the probe, so the app-creation form could not be inspected directly.
evidence.quote: Just a moment... Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue

evidence.claim: A Merge integration guide says that once a partner is approved, Gusto provisions production API credentials and configures scopes for that partner.
evidence.quote: Once approved, Gusto will notify us, provision your Gusto developer account with production API credentials

evidence.claim: A Prismatic connector guide says Gusto keeps new app integrations in a demo environment until production access is approved.
evidence.quote: Gusto restricts new app integrations to a demo environment until the app has been reviewed and approved for production access.

evidence.claim: Information collected during Production Pre-Approval is governed by Gusto's Developer Terms of Service.
evidence.quote: Information collected during pre-approval is handled in accordance with our Developer Terms.

evidence.claim: Gusto says all potential integrations must be vetted and approved, citing the sensitive nature of payroll. The Authentication docs advise getting Pre-Approval approval before investing in a build.
evidence.quote: Due to the sensitive nature of payroll, all potential integrations must be vetted and approved by Gusto.

evidence.claim: After passing QA, Gusto issues production credentials through the Developer Portal.
evidence.quote: After passing QA, Gusto will issue your production credentials via the Developer Portal.

evidence.claim: Gusto's help center says that once a partner is integrated through its API, it is featured in Gusto's in-app directory and on its website. This is a visibility benefit, not a review requirement.
evidence.quote: We feature every integrated partner in our in-app directory and website.

evidence.claim: Gusto's docs say the Introduction's Launch phase involves updating your website or marketplace and publishing support content. No separate listing review is described in that phase.
evidence.quote: You’ll want to update your website or marketplace and publish support content for visibility.

evidence.claim: A Prismatic connector guide says Gusto typically responds to a Production Pre-Approval within 1–2 weeks. This is a third-party claim and has not been confirmed against Gusto's own docs.
evidence.quote: typically responds within 1–2 weeks

evidence.claim: Gusto recommends applying for Production Pre-Approval before building, and says building first is at the developer's own risk because approval is not guaranteed.
evidence.quote: building first is at your own risk

evidence.claim: A Merge blog post says a Gusto security review may include follow-up questions, and that a partner who passes gets its developer account provisioned, production credentials generated, and scopes set up.
evidence.quote: Gusto will perform a security review to validate the controls in place and may ask follow-up questions.

evidence.claim: Pre-approval is needed for implementation support, solution design guidance, and debugging requests, so developers without approval get no Gusto technical help.
evidence.quote: An approved Production Pre-Approval is required for solution design guidance, implementation support, and debugging requests.

evidence.claim: A Gusto Developer Portal account (dev.gusto.com) is required before the Production Pre-Approval application can be completed. The docs do not mention a paid plan, partner program fee, or business verification.
evidence.quote: You must have a Developer Portal account to complete the application.

evidence.claim: Setup order in the Gusto docs: create a developer account, complete Organization setup, create an Application to get sandbox client credentials, then create a demo company to test OAuth.
evidence.quote: Once you’ve created an account and completed your Organization setup, you can then create an application

evidence.claim: In the Embedded Payroll quickstart, the Developer Portal flow is: create an Organization, then an Application. At least one redirect URI is required, and the Application generates a client_id and client_secret. At sign-up, developers must answer 'Are you building embedded payroll?'
evidence.quote: Provide at least one redirect URI (required for OAuth2)

evidence.claim: Developer Portal keys are sandbox-only at first (api.gusto-demo.com). Production keys are issued only after review.
evidence.quote: The API keys initially accessible from Gusto's Developer Portal are for our sandbox environment only

evidence.claim: Redirect URI rules: at least one per app, multiple allowed on one app, and wildcard URIs or URIs with fragments are not supported. Demo redirects can be edited in the Applications tab; production redirect changes go through Gusto support email.
evidence.quote: OAuth2 does not support wildcard URIs or URIs with fragments (e.g #).

open_questions: Gusto does not publish review timelines for Production Pre-Approval, Security Review or QA. The only figure (1-2 weeks for Pre-Approval) comes from a third-party Prismatic guide and is unverified.
Required artifacts for Pre-Approval beyond the Security Review inputs (privacy policy, logo, homepage, demo video) are not stated in the docs. The Pre-Approval form was not readable.
The Developer Portal (dev.gusto.com) and the authorize endpoint sat behind bot checks, so the exact app-creation form fields and the client_id validation message were not seen.
Refresh token lifetime and rotation are not documented; test refresh behavior in the demo environment.
No install or user cap for unreviewed apps was found, but the changelog was only checked through search snippets.

Composio's default scopes (companies:read, employees:read, payrolls:read) are not confirmed against Gusto's API reference, and the Prismatic guide says Gusto scopes are not used there, which conflicts with Gusto's docs. Verify the scope names and what Gusto grants.
Confirm whether you are building for App Integrations or Embedded Payroll. The two have different partner and review paths, and this guide assumes App Integrations.
Common rejection reasons are not documented by Gusto.
The Gusto support email address was not captured in research; get it from the Developer Portal or docs before you need it.
